Rhonda Hamilton

Independent candidate for Mayor of the District of Columbia · Open seat

Mental health advocate (founder and executive director of M.I. Mother's Keeper); former real estate broker and small business owner

Rhonda Hamilton is a third-generation Washingtonian from Southeast D.C. She founded the mental health advocacy nonprofit M.I. Mother's Keeper and spent about 20 years in real estate and finance. She ran a write-in campaign for mayor in 2022, announced an independent bid in December 2025, and appears on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot with Janeese Lewis George (D) and Robert L. Gross (DC Statehood Green).

Where Hamilton stands

Housing
Proposes more affordable, income-restricted subsidized units and more affordable homes for residents who earn too much for housing programs. Also proposes audits of housing waitlists and housing agencies.
Federal intervention and home rule
Supports D.C. statehood or a constitutional amendment to secure home rule. Says she would organize residents and lobbyists to speed up either path.
Immigration enforcement
Says she does not approve of federal immigration enforcement in the District. Says ICE activity has strained police relationships with families.
Public safety
Says she would support law enforcement while requiring accountability and transparency, and opposes over-policing. Proposes an audit of the Metropolitan Police Department.
Youth curfews
Says youth curfews do not work. Argues that a curfew signals the government has no solution, and links youth issues to the cost of living keeping parents at work.
Health care / behavioral health
Proposes integrating behavioral health care and general medical care. Says combining the two would lower costs for patients.
Government accountability
Proposes auditing city agencies in her first days in office to create continuity among them, starting with the housing agencies.

Background

  • Candidate for Mayor of D.C., 2026 general election (Independent)
  • Write-in candidate for Mayor of D.C., 2022 (unsuccessful)
  • Founder and executive director, M.I. Mother's Keeper (mental health advocacy nonprofit), 2015–present
  • Former member, United Planning Organization Health Advisory Council Board
  • Former broker and owner of a Coldwell Banker franchise brokerage in Prince George's County, MD; about 20 years in real estate and finance
  • Attended the University of the District of Columbia (business management), 2002–2004; did not graduate
  • Graduate of Dunbar High School
  • Registered independent since 2012; previously a registered Democrat
